transcript:
Header: Date: 2025-06-03 | Start: 15:00 PT | Duration: ~42 min
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jon (Redwood SE), Tara (Redwood Partnerships), Ethan (VectorEdge Channel Lead), Priya (Solutions Architect), Liam (Sales Director), Sofia (Partner Ops)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for making time — quick agenda: pipeline roll, who owns what, technical next steps, and timeline alignment — Ethan, want to kick us off with a quick rundown of the top two deals?
[00:18] Ethan: yeah sure, thanks Maya. so we've got two priority opps, RetailOne which is a big omni-retail chain, expected ARR north of 1.2M if we convert, and MediCore which is in healthcare, slower procurement but higher expansion potential. RetailOne is furthest along with an initial tech eval slated, MediCore is still legal/procurement heavy.
[00:41] Maya: ok, that's helpful. Liam — can you confirm VectorEdge's expected close windows? any exec sponsor lined up?
[00:49] Liam: RetailOne target is end of July for a PO, but that depends on the performance numbers. We have a champion — head of engineering — but need an exec intro to buyer to lock budget. MediCore is more Q4 likely.
[01:05] Jon: quick Q on the performance numbers you need for RetailOne — is it single-request p99 latency under 400ms or is tail requirement tighter?
[01:12] Priya: p99 under 350 ideally, and they poke at concurrency too — the demo will try 250 concurrent users sim, which translates roughly to 250 qps with short prompts.
[01:25] Jon: ok that aligns with our 8-bit quantized variants; we should define the prompt mix. I'll propose a benchmark plan — can we get a sample prompt set?
[01:35] Priya: yes we'll share a sanitized set by Tuesday.
[01:42] Tara: on crediting — VectorEdge and Redwood agreed to a split for joint-closed deals, we should document the exact referral/credit flow for CRM. Sofia?
[01:50] Sofia: yep, I'll share our lead attribution template. question: do you require modifications on CRM fields to map Redwood as co-sell partner?
[01:58] Maya: ideally yes, we need the lead source and partner touch timestamp so revenue ops can reconcile. If VectorEdge can add partner_account_id we'll map it.
[02:10] Ethan: one tricky bit: RetailOne legal wants certain data residency terms — they're asking about audit logs and encryption key control. MediCore will insist on KMS/HSM.
[02:21] Maya: Redwood's private option and KMS integrations cover HSM scenarios, but we should not overpromise — we'll share the SOC2 and security pack. I'll loop in our security doc.
[02:33] Liam: and on pricing — RetailOne is very price sensitive; we need a sweet spot to be competitive with Anthropic and OpenAI pricing on token cost. How flexible is Redwood on early pilot pricing?
[02:45] Maya: we can do a pilot discount for a limited period, but we'll build the economics slide so VectorEdge can present the net cost after credits. That slide will include per-token cost, estimated monthly token usage, and expected latency SLOs.
[02:58] Priya: for the bench, we need to know if you support continuous batching and some KV cache patterns so that demo reflects production. Any special runtime notes?
[03:08] Jon: yes, our runtime supports KV cache reuse and batch sizing; for RetailOne I'd recommend enabling prefix caching for repeated system prompts — that reduces token spend and latency. We'll show a before/after during the tech deep-dive.
[03:24] Ethan: on roles, can we have a single contact at Redwood for procurement/legal questions to avoid scatter?
[03:31] Maya: that's me for commercial, I'll loop security docs to Tara who owns partnerships compliance. For deep technical and benchmarks it's Jon.
[03:39] Sofia: who will take the lead to draft the co-sell MOU? VectorEdge legal wants to see a brief MOU before engaging CISO.
[03:46] Tara: I can draft a lightweight MOA template and share this week; it will outline revenue split, lead attribution, and liabilities.
[03:54] Liam: perfect. quick question on deal crediting — what if VectorEdge sources the account but Redwood introduces the technical eval, how do we split?
[04:04] Maya: typical approach is partner-first credit with sunset credits for active engagement; exact split we'll propose in the MOU — this goes in the one-pager.
[04:12] Ethan: on the technical POC for RetailOne, they want a 2-week pilot hitting 500 qps in peak sim — is that realistic?
[04:20] Jon: 500 qps with short prompts is doable on dedicated pools but depends on model variant, quantization, and batching. We'll need to run a scaled benchmark — I'm estimating dedicated capacity or a performance tier in hosted with reserved concurrency. We'll outline tradeoffs in the benchmark plan.
[04:39] Priya: MediCore's main blocker is compliance: audit logs, KMS, and data residency. Can Redwood ship Private in time for their timeline?
[04:48] Maya: Private deployments can be on a quarter cadence; for MediCore we'd need a scope call. We shouldn't promise Q3 until we map infra and legal.
[04:58] Ethan: ok understood. next immediate steps?
[05:02] Maya: Jon will own the benchmark plan and runbook; I'll own the economics/one-pager; Tara will draft the MOU; Sofia will export CRM mapping; VectorEdge will share sample prompts and confirm sponsor intros.
[05:18] Liam: any blockers from Redwood side for an exec intro next week?
[05:23] Maya: I can intro to our BD lead, but we prefer an internal 15-min pre-brief before exec intro.
[05:30] Priya: on the POC data — RetailOne wants to test with PII-sanitized samples; we need clarity on what data is allowed in the pilot environment.
[05:41] Tara: we'll add legal to a short follow-up to clarify data handling, but generally pilot data must be sanitized and covered by an NDA.
[05:49] Ethan: last thing — can you include a simple fallback policy in the MOU if SLAs aren't met?
[05:55] Maya: yes we'll include rollback/fallback and credit terms in the MOU draft.
[06:00] Jon: ok I'll send a proposed benchmark matrix — concurrency, prompt mix, seq length, payloads. Expect that by Monday.
[06:08] Maya: great. thanks all — we'll reconvene after items are shared, ideally next check-in w/ benchmarks and MOU in place.
[06:15] Ethan: thanks everyone.

Notes about transcript: some words may be mis-transcribed (e.g., KMS/KHS, queue/QA), and speaker labels near the end had slight overlap where "Speaker 2" showed up in the raw export. This has been lightly cleaned but kept authentic.
